Row 4: Operational Execution Audit & Analyst Questions (Analyst Q&A Highlights)
WINS / DRAGS & ANALYST Q&A
What Management Did Right (Operational Wins)
  • Surpassed $1.0B Revenue Run-Rate: Q3 revenue climbed 40% YoY to $252.44M, establishing Xometry as essential manufacturing infrastructure.
  • Marketplace Growth Surged +42.9% YoY: Marketplace revenue reached $238.00M, driven by 93,812 active buyers and record 4,255 net additions.
  • Adjusted EBITDA Surged 249% YoY: Delivered $21.42M with EBITDA margin expanding 510 bps YoY to 8.5%.
  • GAAP Operating & Net Income Turned Positive: Operating income inflected to $0.06M and net income reached $1.94M.
What Went Wrong & Execution Headwinds
  • Services Segment Growth Sluggish (+2.3% YoY): Services revenue reached $14.44M, showing low sequential momentum compared to core marketplace.
  • Stock Compensation Drag ($11.29M): SBC remains elevated relative to net income, leaving True Free Cash Flow at -$3.42M.
  • Macro Industrial Cyclicality: Capital goods procurement and prototyping remain sensitive to general manufacturing PMIs.
  • Supplier Capacity Staging: Expanding into certified aerospace/defense requires ongoing recruitment of ITAR/CMMC machine shops.
Institutional Conference Call Analyst Questions & Executive Answers (Analyst Q&A)
Brian Peterson (Raymond James) Crossing the $1B Run-Rate & Enterprise Accounts Spending >$50K

Question: Sanjeev, crossing the $1B run rate is a huge milestone. Can you talk about the 26% growth in $50K+ accounts, and how enterprise procurement integrations like TradeCentric are driving larger share of wallet?

Executive Answer: Sanjeev Singh Sahni (CEO) stated: 'Crossing the $1 billion revenue run rate reflects our transformation from a spot quoting tool into essential enterprise supply chain infrastructure. Accounts spending over $50K grew 26% to 2,172, and 98% of our revenue came from existing accounts. With our TradeCentric integration now live across SAP Ariba, Coupa, and Microsoft Dynamics, corporate buyers can route purchase orders seamlessly through Xometry without leaving their native ERP systems.'

Eric Sheridan (Goldman Sachs) AI Sourcing Models, Workcenter Launch & Marketplace Gross Margin

Question: James, marketplace gross margin hit a record 36.0%. How much of that expansion is driven by your new AI pricing algorithms versus supplier network scale, and what is the sustainable margin ceiling?

Executive Answer: James Miln (CFO) responded: 'Our machine learning models continuously ingest supplier capacity, material spot costs, and regional delivery metrics. The 30 bps expansion to 36.0% was directly driven by improved pricing accuracy and automated routing in our new Workcenter portal. While we maintain a long-term target of 35-36%, our growing scale gives us exceptional pricing power and supplier engagement.'

Shawn Harrison (Loop Capital) Aerospace, Defense & Texas Manufacturing Hub Velocity

Question: Sanjeev, you announced a partnership with MxD for CMMC cybersecurity certification and noted Texas partner jobs grew twice the national rate. How is defense and aerospace demand trending given reshoring mandates?

Executive Answer: Sanjeev Singh Sahni explained: 'Defense and aerospace are among our fastest-growing sectors. Prime contractors require ITAR-compliant, CMMC-certified domestic suppliers, and our AI marketplace instantly identifies qualified American machine shops. Our Texas supplier network is expanding rapidly to meet aerospace demand, proving that digital manufacturing is central to the reshoring of the American industrial base.'
